Start Here — Easy Guide

New here? Everything works in 3 easy steps

No account, no download, no sign-up. Every tool on this page works the same way, on any phone, in three steps.

Step 1

Pick a tool

Go to the Tools section and choose what you need — a name, a caption, hashtags, and more. Can't find a tool? Type its name in the search box at the top of the Tools section and it will appear.

Step 2

Type 2–3 words

Type your topic or keyword — for example “coffee shop” or “fitness”. Every box already shows an example, so you can see exactly what to type.

Step 3

Tap Generate, then Copy

Tap Generate and your results appear at once. Tap Copy on the one you like and paste it anywhere — WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, or your own website.

Having trouble opening or reading the page? The Questions section covers the common problems and their fixes — the page not opening inside WhatsApp, text looking too small, or the Copy button not working.

    Rank Power

    How real visitors help this site rank on Google

    Google does not rank tricks — it ranks real activity by real people: daily visits, time spent on the page, tools used for real work, and the site's name mentioned out in the world. There are no fake clicks and no shortcuts here. If every visitor does one small real thing each day, the ranking follows.

    Visit every day

    Open Success Hub each morning and read today's mission. Visitors who return daily are the clearest signal to Google that a site is alive and useful.

    How new websites rank on Google in 30 days

    1. Find long-tail keywords with the Keyword Finder.
    2. Write titles under 60 characters with the SEO Writer.

    Rozgar

    How to find a real job and avoid fake job offers

    A real job pays you — you never pay for it. Fake offers ask for a “registration fee”, “security deposit” or training charges first, and disappear with your money. Before you accept any job: check the employer is real (visit the shop or office, ask people who work there), agree the salary and payday in clear words, and meet for the first time in a public place or at the workplace itself — never send money, an OTP or a password to anyone for a job.

    1. Never pay any fee for a job — real employers pay you.
    2. Check the employer: real shop or office, real workers.
    3. Fix the salary, hours and payday before you start.
    4. Find real jobs in the Rozgar Office
    Free Food

    Free food for the poor — how to ask, and how to give

    If your family needs food, there is no shame in asking — asking honestly is how help finds you. Post your appeal in Free Food for the Poor: your name, how many family members, your city and area, and exactly what food you need — and if you can, record a short video in your own voice, because people help faster when they can see and hear the real need. If you want to give: open an appeal, read the full detail, and call or WhatsApp the family directly — give the food with your own hands, or arrange it with a nearby shop, and never send money to any middleman.

    1. Needy family: post the appeal with photo or video, family members, city and what food is needed.
    2. Helper: read the full detail and comments, then call or WhatsApp the family directly.
    3. Give food directly — cooked food, ration, or a shop arranged by you. No fee, no middleman, ever.
    4. Open Free Food for the Poor
    Shopping Guide

    Every kind of shopping: clear rules and ranked picks

    A shopping mistake wastes real money. Below are clear rules for every kind of shopping, clothing brands ranked with the reason for each rank, and honest brand-vs-brand comparisons — so you can get the highest quality at the lowest price. Prices are shown as levels (Low / Mid / High) because they change by city and by sale; always confirm the final price at the shop or on the brand's official website.

    Today's shopping tip — Today

    Loading…

    The Golden Rules — remember these 8 before any shopping

    1. List first, shop second. Without a list you buy extras and forget the essentials.
    2. Fix your budget first. Set your total limit before you go — and do not cross it.
    3. Compare the price in 3 places. Check three prices for the same item, then buy.
    4. A sale does not always mean cheap. Compare the old price and the sale price — both.
    5. Quality once, cheap again and again. For things you use daily, spend on quality.
    6. Keep the bill and warranty card. Without them, exchange and claims become difficult.
    7. Check the seller's rating online. Always read the reviews, items sold and return policy.
    8. Never decide in a hurry. A “today only” offer is usually there tomorrow too.

    Buy Winter Clothes Smartly — 6 Checks Before You Pay

    A winter piece is bought once and used for months. These six checks take two minutes in the shop and save real money:

    Fabric & Warmth

    • Check the fabric: wool and wool-blend pieces are the warmest; acrylic is a good cheaper option. Thin, shiny polyester looks warm but lets cold air through.
    • Test the warmth: hold the fabric up to the light — if light passes through easily, cold air will too. A heavier piece is usually a warmer piece.
    • For jackets, check the inner lining and padding: even, thick padding with no empty gaps is what keeps you warm.

    Stitching & Fit

    • Check the stitching: pull the seams gently — tight, even stitches with no loose threads. Loose stitching opens up in the first wash.
    • On jackets, test every zip and button in the shop; a broken zip makes the warmest jacket useless.
    • Buy one size with room: winter clothes are worn over other clothes, so a tight fit feels colder and wears out faster.

    Timing & Wash Care

    • Buy early: shop in October–November, before the cold peaks. In December–January the same jacket costs more, and the best sizes finish first.
    • The other smart time is the end-of-season sale (late January–February): buy next winter's clothes at the lowest price of the year.
    • Read the wash care label before buying: wool shawls and sweaters often need a gentle hand wash or dry clean — if you cannot care for it, choose an easy-wash acrylic piece instead.

    Winter Shopping — Quick Questions

    Which jacket is best for very cold areas like Murree or the northern areas?

    A thick puffer jacket with full inner padding — the kind Outfitters and Breakout sell — plus a wool shawl or muffler for the neck. In very cold areas, layers beat one thin jacket: sweater inside, puffer outside. Expect to pay roughly Rs 4,500 – 9,000 for a good puffer; prices change by shop and season.

    What is a fair shawls price in Pakistan?

    It depends on the fabric. A simple local-market shawl is about Rs 500 – 1,500, a good branded wool-blend shawl (Bonanza Satrangi, Khaadi) is about Rs 1,200 – 6,500, and a premium Gul Ahmed or pure wool shawl can be Rs 8,000 or more. These are ranges, not fixed prices — always confirm at the shop, and compare in 3 places first.

    Which brand gives warm sweaters at the lowest price?

    Bonanza Satrangi in a sale is the best value among the warm sweaters brands — roughly Rs 1,800 – 4,000 for a sweater. The local bazaar is cheaper still (about Rs 800 – 2,000), but check the fabric and stitching piece by piece, because quality varies.

    When should I buy winter clothes to save money?

    Twice a year: early, in October–November before prices rise with the cold, or at the end-of-season sale in late January–February, when shops clear winter stock at the lowest prices. Buying in the middle of a cold December week is the most expensive way to do winter shopping in Pakistan.

    Grocery Savings Plan — Save on a Full Month of Groceries

    Groceries are the one bill every family pays every month — and the one where small habits quietly take the most money. This plan compares the places honestly: where a month of groceries costs least, where quality is surest, and the simple per-kg check that shows the real price of any pack, big or small. The savings notes below are honest, typical comparisons of the same items in different places; prices change by city and by week, so run the per-kg check yourself before you pay.

    1
    Cheapest — Bulk Staples & Fresh

    Wholesale Market & Sabzi Mandi

    Reason: Atta, rice, daal, sugar, oil and fresh vegetables sell here at near-trade prices, because you are buying close to the source. The same monthly staples cost visibly more when bought in small packs from small shops.

    Best for: One monthly trip for bulk staples, and the weekly fresh vegetables and fruit run.

    Price: LowestBest for: bulk staples & fresh produce

    Best for: One monthly trip for branded items, especially during offer days.

    Cheapest Fresh — One Day a Week

    Weekly Bazaar (Itwar / Juma Bazaar)

    Reason: Vegetable and fruit sellers compete side by side, so fresh prices drop — and late in the day, sellers often cut prices further on stock they do not want to carry back.

    Best for: The weekly fruit and vegetable shop on a tight budget.

    Big Supermarket

    Price: MiddleBest for: fixed prices & offers

    Local Kiryana Shop

    Reason: Two minutes from home, and many kiryana shops give udhaar (credit) to families they know — real help in a hard week. But per-item prices are usually the highest of all, and small packs cost the most per kg.

    Best for: Daily small needs — milk, eggs, bread — not the monthly shop.

    Price: Highest per itemBest for: daily small needs
    6
    Most Convenient — Check the Total

    Online Grocery Apps

    Reason: Delivered to your door with tempting banner offers — but delivery charges and higher per-item prices can quietly eat the saving. Compare the final total at checkout, never the banner discount.

    Best for: Busy families, and heavy items you do not want to carry.

    Comfort: HighestCheck: final total with delivery

    Final verdict: The cheapest month is a split shop: staples in bulk from the wholesale market, fresh from the sabzi mandi or weekly bazaar, and branded items on offer at a cash & carry. The kiryana shop is for daily small needs, and online grocery only wins when the final total — delivery included — is still lower.

    Simple formula: Bulk = wholesale · Fresh = mandi / weekly bazaar · Branded = offers. And whatever the shop, compare the per-kg or per-litre price, not the pack price — and check any "sale" price in seconds with the Discount Calculator.

    Save on Groceries — Smart Checks Before You Pay

    The plan above picks the shop; these checks protect the money inside any shop:

    The List & the Plan

    • Write the list at home from what has actually finished — not from memory in the shop. Grocery shopping without a list usually costs 20–30% extra.
    • Shop on a rhythm: once a month for staples, once a week for fresh. Every extra trip is extra spending.
    • Never shop hungry, and keep last month's bill — compare the two totals, month to month.

    In the Shop

    • Compare the per-kg / per-litre price, never the pack price — a bigger packet is not always cheaper per kg.
    • Check the expiry date on everything; the packet at the back of the shelf is often the freshest.
    • Buy seasonal vegetables and fruit: cheapest, freshest, and they travel the shortest distance.

    At Home — Stop the Waste

    • Store atta, rice and daal in airtight containers the day they arrive, so nothing spoils or gets insects.
    • Cook with what expires first; freeze extra roti, vegetables and cooked food instead of throwing them away.
    • Wasted food is the most expensive grocery of all — the saving you threw in the bin earns nothing.

    Grocery Savings — Quick Questions

    How much can a family really save with a grocery plan?

    In most homes, a large part of the monthly grocery bill — often 15–30% — goes on impulse buying, wrong pack sizes and food that spoils before it is used. This plan attacks exactly those three leaks: list first, per-kg check, bulk staples, no waste. The honest test is your own bill: compare next month's total with this month's, and that difference is your real saving.

    Wholesale market or supermarket — which is cheaper for monthly groceries?

    For staples and fresh produce, the wholesale market and sabzi mandi are cheaper. For labelled branded items on offer — and for saving time with sure expiry dates — the supermarket or cash & carry can win. That is why many families split the month: one wholesale trip for staples, one supermarket trip for branded items.

    Is a bigger pack always cheaper?

    No — only the per-kg price tells the truth. Example: a 1 kg pack at Rs 210 costs Rs 210 per kg; a 5 kg pack at Rs 950 costs Rs 190 per kg, so the big pack wins. But a "family pack" of 5 kg at Rs 1,100 is Rs 220 per kg — there, the small pack wins. Divide the price by the weight before you decide; it takes five seconds.

    When is the best time to buy fresh vegetables and fruit?

    Early morning at the sabzi mandi, when the fresh stock arrives and the choice is widest — or late in the weekly bazaar, when sellers cut prices on perishable stock rather than carry it back. In both cases, seasonal items are the cheapest and freshest choice.

    8 Practical Ways to Save on Groceries in Pakistan

    Eight habits, in the order a family actually shops — where to go, what to buy, how to check the price, and how to make the food last. Together they are the whole Grocery Savings Plan in one list:

    1. Split the shop — weekly sabzi mandi vs supermarket. Buy fresh vegetables and fruit once a week from the sabzi mandi or weekly bazaar, where fresh prices sit in the lowest band. Keep the supermarket or cash & carry for one monthly trip for branded and packed items. One shop cannot be cheapest at everything.
    2. Buy seasonal vegetables and fruit. Whatever is in season fills every stall, travels the shortest distance and costs least — and it is fresher and tastier too. Out-of-season items are stored or imported, so they sit in a higher price band.
    3. Buy staples in bulk, once a month. Atta, chawal (rice), daal, sugar, ghee and cooking oil keep for weeks — buying them in bigger packs from the wholesale market or a cash & carry usually gives the lowest per-kg price. Small weekly packs from the kiryana shop cost the most per kg.
    4. Always shop with a written list. Write the list at home from what has actually finished, and buy only what is on it. Grocery shopping without a list usually costs 20–30% extra, because the extras are decided by the shop, not by you.
    5. Compare the per-kg and per-litre price, never the pack price. Divide the price by the weight before you decide — a bigger pack is not always cheaper per kg, and a “family pack” can quietly cost more. Five seconds of maths beats every banner in the shop.
    6. Avoid impulse buys and ready-made items. Snacks at the counter, cold drinks and ready-made meals are priced for convenience, not value — the same food cooked at home costs far less per serving. Eat before you shop, and keep ready-made items as a treat, not a habit.
    7. Store food properly so nothing is wasted. Move atta, rice and daal into airtight containers the day they arrive, cook with what expires first, and freeze extra roti, vegetables and cooked food instead of throwing them away. Wasted food is the most expensive grocery of all.
    8. Run one simple monthly budget. Fix a single monthly grocery total, work out your weekly and daily allowance with the Grocery Budget Calculator below, and keep each bill. Compare this month's total with last month's — that difference is your real saving, and it tells you if the plan is working.

    Grocery Budget — More Questions

    How do I make a simple monthly grocery budget that actually works?

    Fix one monthly total first, then split it with the Grocery Budget Calculator in this guide: it shows your weekly allowance (monthly × 12 ÷ 52) and your daily allowance (monthly × 12 ÷ 365). Spend staples money once a month, fresh money once a week, and keep last month's bill to compare — if this month's total is lower, the budget is working.

    Why are seasonal vegetables cheaper and better?

    When a vegetable is in season, every mandi and bazaar is full of it, supply is high and it travels a short distance — so its price band drops and the vegetable is fresher and tastier. Out-of-season vegetables are stored or brought from far away, which pushes them into a higher price band.

    How much do I save if I cut 10% of my grocery spending?

    Exactly 10% of your monthly budget, every month — and twelve times that in a year. Type your monthly grocery budget into the Grocery Budget Calculator in this guide and it works out your 10% monthly saving and your yearly saving for you, with no guessing.

    Sabzi mandi, supermarket or online grocery — which one should I choose?

    Choose by the job: the sabzi mandi for fresh vegetables and fruit at the lowest price band, the supermarket for fixed prices, sure expiry dates and branded offers, and online grocery only when the final checkout total — delivery included — is still lower. The comparison table in this guide shows the Low / Mid / High price bands side by side; prices change by city and week, so always check before you buy.

    Rules for Every Kind of Shopping

    Each category has its own rules, and using the wrong category's rules wastes money. Remember these:

    Clothing Rules

    • Feel the fabric by hand — thin fabric tears quickly, and very thick fabric is uncomfortable in summer.
    • Check the colour in daylight; shop lighting changes how a colour looks.
    • Buying unstitched? Confirm the measurements and extra fabric (shirt and shalwar separately) first.
    • Buy in a sale if you like, but always compare with the old price first.
    • Wash new clothes separately the first time — the colour can run.

    Shoes Rules

    • Try shoes in the evening — feet swell slightly during the day, so the true size shows then.
    • Wear both shoes and walk in them, not just one.
    • Bend the sole — a very stiff sole will hurt your feet.
    • For everyday shoes, choose comfort over price.

    Mobile & Electronics Rules

    • Buy only with an official warranty — a cheap phone without one costs more later.
    • Match the IMEI / serial number on the box and on the device.
    • Check the price in 3 shops and on the official website.
    • An older model in a sale is a smart buy if it does the same job.
    • Get the warranty date written on the bill.

    Grocery Rules

    • Check the expiry date on everything — the packet at the back is often fresher.
    • Compare the per-kg / per-litre price; a bigger packet is not always cheaper.
    • Grocery shopping without a list always means extra spending.
    • Do not shop while hungry — you will buy things you do not need.

    Online Shopping Rules

    • Check the seller's rating, reviews and number of items sold first.
    • Prefer Cash on Delivery (COD) — the item in your hand first, then the money.
    • Always check the size chart; online sizes can differ from shop sizes.
    • Read the return / exchange policy before you order.
    • Be suspicious of a deal that is far too cheap — it may be a copy or a fake.

    Beauty & Skin Rules

    • Buy original products only from a trusted shop or the official store — copies damage skin.
    • Try a small pack first; buy the large one only if it suits you.
    • Always read the ingredients and the expiry date.
    • Every skin is different — what suits a friend may not suit you.

    Khaana Peena — Food, Drink & Kitchen Staples Compared

    The kitchen is where a family spends every single day. These four daily items — cooking oil, milk, tea and atta — look simple, but the wrong daily choice quietly costs money and health all year. Here is each one compared honestly.

    Why compare? These are not one-time purchases — oil, milk, tea and atta are bought every week and eaten every day, so a small mistake repeats itself hundreds of times a year: the wrong oil quietly loads the family with saturated fat, mixed milk carries a daily risk, and refined atta removes the fibre from every single roti. Compare the daily items once, and the right choice works for your health and your budget all year.

    Cooking Oil — Which Oil for Daily Cooking?

    OptionBest forPrice bandWhy it wins or loses
    Canola oilDaily cooking for the whole familyMidLow in saturated fat, neutral taste, works in almost every dish. The balanced everyday oil — it loses only where a strong traditional flavour is the whole point of the dish.
    Sunflower oilFrying and general cookingMidLight taste and handles high heat well, so it is a safe all-rounder. It loses to canola on balance — no real health edge, just a familiar name.
    Mustard oil (sarson)Pickles, fish, strong-flavour desi dishesMidStrong flavour and a high smoke point — unbeatable for pickles and traditional cooking. It loses as an all-day oil because its sharp taste takes over light dishes.
    Desi gheeParathas, halwa, daal tarka, special dishesHighThe best taste and aroma of all — nothing replaces it in a paratha or halwa. It loses as a daily oil: highest in saturated fat and the most expensive on this list.

    BEST CHOICE Canola oil for daily cooking. Reason: it is low in saturated fat, its taste stays out of the way, and one oil covers the whole kitchen — salan, frying and roti work alike. Keep desi ghee for special dishes, in small amounts, where its flavour is the reason for the dish.

    Milk — Full Cream, Low Fat, Packaged or Fresh?

    OptionBest forPrice bandWhy it wins or loses
    Packaged full-cream milkDoodh patti tea, kheer and dessertsHighSealed, expiry-dated and the same quality every time — no water-mixing risk. Rich taste for tea and desserts. It loses on price: it costs more than fresh milk.
    Fresh milk (khulla doodh)Daily home use from a trusted dairyMidFull natural taste and a fair price when the dairy is honest. It loses the moment the source is not trusted — water mixing is common, and there is no expiry date to protect you.
    Packaged low-fat milkWeight care and daily drinkingMidLess fat and fewer calories, still sealed and safe. It loses on taste — tea feels thin and desserts lose their richness.

    BEST CHOICE Packaged milk from a known brand for most homes. Reason: the seal and the printed expiry date remove the biggest risk in milk — mixing. Fresh milk becomes the best choice only when your dairy is fully trusted, because then you get the same safety with better taste at a lower price.

    Tea — Doodh Patti or Green Tea?

    OptionBest forPrice bandWhy it wins or loses
    Doodh patti (milk tea)Morning energy, taste and guestsLowFull taste, filling, and the cup Pakistan runs on. It loses on health only when it is loaded with sugar and repeated many times a day — the tea is fine, the sugar is the problem.
    Green tea (qahwa)After heavy meals and weight careMidLight, needs no milk or sugar, and sits easy after a heavy meal. It loses on taste for doodh patti lovers and never gives that full, satisfying feeling.

    BEST CHOICE Doodh patti in the morning, green tea after heavy meals. Reason: the morning cup is about taste and energy, and doodh patti wins there — just keep the sugar low. After a heavy meal the need changes to lightness, and that is exactly where green tea wins.

    Atta — Whole Wheat or Refined?

    OptionBest forPrice bandWhy it wins or loses
    Whole wheat atta (chakki atta)Daily roti for the whole familyMidThe full grain stays in, so the fibre stays in: it keeps you full longer and is kinder to blood sugar. The honest everyday winner for a food eaten three times a day.
    Refined flour (maida / fine atta)Naan, bakery items and special cookingLowSoft, white and cheap — right for naan and bakery work. It loses for daily use because refining removes the fibre, so it fills you less and raises sugar faster.

    BEST CHOICE Whole wheat chakki atta for daily roti. Reason: roti is eaten every day, so its fibre works for you every day — fuller stomach, steadier energy. Keep maida for the special items it is actually made for.

    Reference: General nutrition guidance followed by doctors and diet experts — pick daily oils low in saturated fat, whole grains over refined flour, and keep added sugar low. General guidance only, not a medical prescription.

    Bakra / Goat Buying — Qurbani & Farming Guide

    A bakra is one of the biggest single purchases of the year, and the mandi is full of tricks. Buy with checks, not with hope: age first, health second, breed third — and never in a hurry.

    Why compare? A goat cannot be returned. Pay for a painted coat, water-filled weight or a too-young animal and the whole Qurbani budget is lost in one evening — and a sick animal can fail the Qurbani itself. Comparing breeds, sellers and health checks before you pay is the only protection a buyer has: ten minutes of checking guards one of the biggest purchases of your year.

    Step 1 — The Age Check: Teeth Tell the Truth

    Open the mouth and count the permanent front teeth yourself. 2 teeth (do dant) means the goat has reached about a year or more — the right age for Qurbani. A goat with only milk teeth is too young, whatever the seller says; a much older goat gives tougher meat. The teeth cannot be faked easily, which is why this check comes first.

    Step 2 — The Health Checks (with the reason for each)

    • Eyes — clear and bright. Dull, watery or red eyes are an early sign of fever and weakness; a healthy goat watches you with shining eyes.
    • Nose — clean and slightly moist. A dry, hot nose, or a running nose, is a sickness sign. Reason: the nose shows breathing trouble before anything else does.
    • Walk — free and straight. Make it walk and run a few steps. A limp or a lazy, dragging walk can hide a leg injury or deep weakness that costs you later.
    • Skin and coat — smooth, no wounds, no lumps. Run your hand over the body and check under the coat. Reason: skin shows parasites, ticks and disease first, before they reach the meat.
    • Teeth — exactly 2 permanent teeth. This proves the age, as explained above — never accept the seller's word in place of your own eyes.
    • Eating — chewing and chewing the cud. A goat that eats well and chews its cud has a working stomach. A goat off its feed is not a well goat, even if it looks fat.

    Step 3 — Breeds Compared: Size and Meat

    OptionBest forPrice bandWhy it wins or loses
    BeetalQurbani and meat — the big-size choiceHighThe famous Punjab breed: big body, more meat, strong look for Qurbani. It loses on cost — the highest price here, and a big goat also eats more while you keep it.
    KamoriFarming and breedingHighThe Sindh breed with long ears and a strong frame — valued for breeding and for milk with meat. Pure bloodlines are expensive, so it wins for farming, not for a one-day Qurbani budget.
    BarbariMeat with faster growthMidGrows fast, adjusts to new places well and gives good meat for its size. It loses to Beetal on sheer size, but wins on value for money.
    TeddySmall homes and first-time keepersLowSmall, hardy and cheap to feed — the easiest goat to keep at home. It loses on meat quantity simply because the animal itself is small.

    Step 4 — Where to Buy: Mandi or Farm?

    OptionBest forPrice bandWhy it wins or loses
    Known farmSure health and known historyHighThe goat's age, feed and health history are known, and the farm's name is at stake if it cheats you. It loses on price and on choice — fewer animals to pick from.
    Mandi (livestock market)Wide choice and bargainingMidMany animals in one place and prices move with bargaining. It loses on safety: sick and weak animals are also sold here, so every check above is fully your own job.

    Fraud Warnings — Read Before You Pay

    • Painted goat: colour is applied to make an ordinary goat look like a rare breed. Rub the coat with a wet cloth or wet hand — fake colour comes off.
    • Water-filled weight: some sellers push excess water or feed just before sale so the belly looks swollen and the weight reads high; the weight falls at home. Judge the body and health, never one-day weight.
    • Age lies: a young goat sold as full-age. Count the teeth yourself — 2 permanent teeth is the proof, not the seller's promise.
    • The rushed night deal: sick animals are mixed into healthy groups and sold in a hurry after dark. Check every animal separately, in daylight, one by one.

    BEST CHOICE A healthy 2-teeth goat from a known farm — or from a trusted mandi seller — with every health check passed. Reason: the 2 teeth prove the right Qurbani age, the clear eyes, clean nose, free walk, clean skin and good appetite prove the health, and a seller whose name is known cannot afford to cheat you. Breed comes after health: a healthy Barbari or Teddy beats a sick Beetal every time.

    Reference: General guidance from experienced farmers and livestock vets — age is judged by the teeth, and health by the eyes, nose, walk, skin and appetite. For a sick animal, always ask a vet.

    Best Shampoo — Picked by Hair Type

    There is no single best shampoo in the market — there is only the best shampoo for your scalp. Match the shampoo to the hair problem first; the brand comes second.

    Why compare? The wrong shampoo does not just waste money — it works against your hair every wash: a strong anti-dandruff formula on dry hair strips it further, and a rich moisturising shampoo on an oily, flaky scalp feeds the flakes. Compare by hair and scalp type first, and the bottle you buy actually treats your problem instead of adding to it.

    OptionBest forPrice bandWhy it wins or loses
    Head & ShouldersOily hair with dandruffMidBuilt for the scalp, not just the hair: its anti-dandruff formula (zinc pyrithione) fights flakes and the itch at the root. It loses for dry hair, where it can feel too strong.
    ClearOily hair with dandruffMidAlso made for dandruff and an oily scalp, with a cool, clean finish. Between Clear and Head & Shoulders, the winner is whichever one your own scalp answers better.
    DoveDry, rough and damaged hairMidMoisturising care that leaves dry hair soft instead of stripped. It loses for very oily hair, where its richness can feel heavy and flat.
    SunsilkDry to normal hair, daily shineLowMoisturising everyday care at the lowest price here. A good daily shampoo for dry-to-normal hair; it is not a dandruff treatment, so it loses where flakes are the real problem.
    PanteneHair fall and weak, breaking hairMidStrength-focused care for hair that breaks and falls. Honest note: hair fall also comes from food, stress and health — shampoo supports the hair, it cannot fix the root cause alone.
    Any mild shampooNormal hair, no scalp problemLowIf the scalp is calm and the hair is normal, a gentle mild shampoo is enough — paying more buys fragrance, not health.

    BEST CHOICE The shampoo matched to your scalp. Reason: dandruff and oil are scalp problems, so Head & Shoulders or Clear wins there; dryness is a hair problem, so moisturising Dove wins there; weak, falling hair needs strength care, so Pantene wins there. The need decides — the brand only follows.

    Reference: Dermatologists advise choosing shampoo by hair and scalp type, not by brand name. If dandruff or hair fall stays severe, see a skin doctor instead of changing bottles again and again.

    Reference: Dermatologists advise choosing soap by skin type, not by advertisement. For a skin problem that does not settle, see a skin doctor.

    Best Hotel — Hotel Types Compared

    A hotel is not a room — it is your family's safety, sleep and food, bought in advance, from photos. The star on the board matters less than what the type of stay actually gives you. Compare the types first; then run the booking checks.

    Why compare? Book the wrong type and you pay luxury money for a plain bed — or save small money and lose the whole trip to noise, dirt and bad food. Two minutes of comparison protects the full booking.

    OptionBest forPrice bandWhy it wins or loses
    Luxury 5-star hotelSpecial stays and honoured guestsHighEverything handled: top comfort, trained service, the best food and full facilities in one place. It loses on one point only — the price. On a routine trip you pay for polish you never use.
    Mid-range 4-star hotelFamily stays and business tripsMidThe balance winner: real comfort, good locations, professional service and proper food at a price a family can actually pay. It loses a little polish against 5-star — and nothing that matters on a real trip.
    Budget 3-star / guest houseShort stays and tight budgetsLowA clean bed, a lock on the door and the basics covered at the lowest price. It loses on service depth and food choice, and quality swings the most here — the booking checks below matter most for this type.

    Before You Book — 4 Checks That Protect Your Money

    • Cleanliness. Read the newest guest reviews and look at guest photos, not hotel photos. A clean bathroom in a recent guest photo tells the truth a shiny lobby cannot.
    • Location. Measure the distance to your real work — the hospital, the office, the family home. A cheap room far away charges you back in taxi fares and tired hours.
    • Reviews. Trust the pattern of recent reviews, not one angry post or one glowing one. The last season's pattern is the hotel you will actually get.
    • Cancellation. Book only where the cancellation terms are written and fair. Plans change; a booking that cannot move is a fine waiting to happen.

    BEST CHOICE Best for family stay: a serviced apartment. Reason: space for everyone and a kitchen for the children — over a few days it beats a hotel room on comfort and cost together.

    BEST CHOICE Best budget trip: a budget 3-star or guest house — after the 4 checks. Reason: the lowest band is safe money only when cleanliness, location, reviews and cancellation are checked first.

    BEST CHOICE Best overall: a mid-range 4-star hotel. Reason: comfort, service, location and price in balance — the stay most families and travellers actually need.

    Best Hostel — Hostel Types Compared

    A hostel is not a cheap hotel — it is where a student studies, a worker sleeps and a traveller rests between roads. The right type gives safety, food and quiet at a low band; the wrong type quietly takes all three away.

    Why compare? Hostel rent is paid month after month, and a bad hostel eats your study, your sleep and your health in silence. Compare the type before the building — the type decides your daily life.

    OptionBest forPrice bandWhy it wins or loses
    Student hostelStudents near college and universityLowBuilt for study life: mess food, shared rooms and rules that keep the place quiet at study hours, at the lowest monthly band. It loses on privacy — rooms are shared and space is tight.
    Working-professionals hostelJob holders and office workersMidA step up in quiet and food: fewer beds per room, better laundry, and timings that suit office life. It loses on price — the monthly band stands above student hostels.
    Travellers / backpackers hostelShort stays, tourists and road travellersLowThe cheapest bed in the city, usually near the centre and the stations, with a social common room. It loses on quiet and privacy — a resting place for days, not a home for months.
    Girls hostelGirls and women — safety firstMidRun for one purpose: safety. A warden on site, visitor rules, secure entry and timings that protect the residents. It loses on freedom of timing — the rules are strict, and that strictness is exactly the point.

    Safety First — Checks Before You Pay Any Hostel

    • Warden and rules. A warden on site, written rules and a proper visitor system. No warden means nobody answers at 2 AM.
    • Locks and entry. Your room and your locker must lock, and the main entry must stay controlled at night. Check with your own hands, not the brochure.
    • Food and water. Eat one mess meal before you decide, and check the drinking water. Hostel health is decided in the kitchen, not in the room.
    • Talk to residents. Ask two or three people already living there. Residents tell you in one minute what no owner will tell you in an hour.
    • See it in person. Visit the exact room — at night if you can — before any advance is paid. Photos lie; your own eyes do not.

    BEST CHOICE Best for students: a student hostel. Reason: the lowest band with food, quiet hours and fellow students around — built for exactly the life a student lives.

    BEST CHOICE Best for workers: a working-professionals hostel. Reason: quieter rooms, better food and office-friendly timings — you pay a little more and sleep a lot better.

    BEST CHOICE Best for travellers: a backpackers hostel. Reason: the cheapest central bed for a few nights — pay for the road ahead, not for a room you only sleep in.

    BEST CHOICE Best for girls: a girls hostel. Reason: warden, visitor rules and secure entry — where safety is the question, this is the only honest answer.

    Beef / chicken karahiGuests and weekend family mealsMidCooked fresh in the wok and eaten from the karahi itself — meat, tomato and green chilli with nothing hidden. It loses on time and price: it must be cooked fresh, and good meat costs.
    NihariSlow weekends and special breakfastsMidSlow-cooked for hours until the gravy turns to silk — the deepest taste on this list. It loses on health and hour: rich, heavy food that belongs to a slow morning, not a daily dinner.
    BBQ — tikka & malai botiParties and evening gatheringsMidSmoke, charcoal and spice: the party plate everyone gathers around, from sharp tikka to soft malai boti. It loses as daily food — it needs charcoal, skill and an occasion.
    Daal + rotiDaily health and the tightest budgetLowThe honest winner of everyday life: light, full of protein, kind to the stomach — the cheapest full meal here. It loses at a dawat: nobody's heart jumps for daal when guests are coming.
    CharghaLahori parties and big family spreadsMidA whole chicken, steamed then fried, standing in the middle of the table — one chargha feeds a group, with full show. It loses on effort and oil: a whole chicken, real work, and a deep fry.

    BEST CHOICE Best for family dinner: chicken biryani. Reason: one deg, full taste, everyone fed — the surest plate a family table knows.

    BEST CHOICE Best for a party: BBQ — tikka and malai boti. Reason: cooked live over charcoal while the guests gather — the food and the event are the same thing. Chargha stands right beside it for a Lahori-style spread.

    BEST CHOICE Best for health: daal + roti. Reason: light, protein-rich and easy on the stomach — the meal you can eat every day and stay well.

    BEST CHOICE Best overall: chicken biryani. Reason: taste, sharing and price in one dish — that is why it tops the ranking and every guest list in the country.

    Reference: General food knowledge of Pakistani kitchens — taste, sharing and the occasion decide the dish. Health guidance is the common advice of doctors: keep rich, oily dishes occasional and daily food light. Cook to your own family's taste.

    Kapra Comparison — Which Fabric Wins, and Why

    Six fabrics run almost every wardrobe in Pakistan. None of them wins everything — each one wins its own season and its own job. Find your need in the table; that row is your answer.

    FabricBest forPrice bandWhy it wins / why it is better than the others
    CottonDaily wear, all year — shirts, shalwar kameez, home wearMidThe all-rounder: a natural fibre that breathes, absorbs sweat and washes easily, so it beats synthetics on comfort every single day. It loses to lawn on extreme-heat lightness and to khaddar on winter warmth — it is the balanced middle, not the extreme.
    LawnSummer wear — above all women's summer suitsMidThe summer winner: the finest, lightest weave of cotton, so air passes through and the body stays cool when no other fabric can cope. It loses on strength — the fine weave is delicate, wrinkles fast and needs gentle washing.
    KhaddarWinter daily wear — warm suits that last for seasonsMidThe winter workhorse: a thick, tightly woven cotton that holds warmth and takes hard daily use year after year — it beats thinner fabrics on life. It loses completely in summer: wear khaddar in June and you will understand why.
    SilkFormal and festive wear — weddings, parties, giftsHighThe shine winner: a natural sheen, a smooth fall and a premium feel that no everyday fabric can copy — for one special day, nothing here beats it. It loses on price and on care: it stains easily and often needs dry cleaning.
    WoolPeak winter — sweaters, coats, shawls for cold areasHighThe warmth winner: wool traps body heat better than any other fabric on this list, so in real cold it has no rival. It loses on weight, on care, and on the calendar — most of Pakistan needs it for only a few weeks a year.
    Georgette / ChiffonParty wear, dupattas and flowing outfitsMidThe fall winner: light, flowing and elegant in movement — the drape is the whole point, and no stiff fabric gives it. It loses on coverage and strength: it is often see-through, needs a lining, and its stitching must be fine or the seams tear.

    BEST CHOICE For summer: lawn. Reason: in real heat the finest weave wins — lawn is the lightest, coolest fabric here, and summer comfort is decided by how much air the cloth lets through.

    BEST CHOICE For daily wear, all year: cotton. Reason: it breathes, absorbs sweat, washes easily and survives daily use — the one fabric that never has a wrong season for everyday clothes.

    BEST CHOICE For winter: khaddar for daily wear, wool for peak cold. Reason: khaddar's thick weave gives warmth with hard-wearing life at a mid price; wool is warmer still, but its price and care only make sense where the cold is serious.

    Reference: General fabric knowledge used by cloth merchants and tailors — natural fibres breathe better than synthetics, a tighter weave lasts longer, and the right fabric is always the one matched to the season. Prices move by city and shop, so this guide uses price bands only — check the fresh price before you pay.

    Lawn vs cotton vs khaddar — fabric quality checksWatch on YouTube Fabric comparison blogs — lawn, cotton, khaddarRead blogs on Chrome

    Mera kapra behtar kyun hai? — Judge any seller's claim in 6 checks

    1. Fabric — what is it really made of? Pure cotton, lawn or khaddar breathes; a cheap synthetic mix shines more but sticks to the body and pills fast. Ask the fabric name — a seller who cannot name it cannot claim it is better.
    2. Weave — hold it to the light. A tight, even weave lasts for years; a loose weave with gaps stretches out of shape in months. The weave, not the shine, decides the cloth's life.
    3. Colour fastness — the wet-cloth test. Rub a wet white cloth on a hidden corner. If colour comes off, the colour will bleed in the first wash — however beautiful it looks today.
    4. Stitching — straight and strong. On stitched suits, check the seams: straight lines, small even stitches, no loose threads. Fine stitching is where cheap kapra is caught.
    5. Fall — how it drapes. Hold the cloth up and let it fall. Good kapra falls smooth and even; poor kapra twists, curls at the edges and fights the body.
    6. Season — right cloth, right weather. The “best” kapra in the wrong season is the wrong kapra: lawn in January and khaddar in June both fail, whatever their quality.

    1%
    The 1% rule: on every deal, the buyer receives 1% — paid by the seller

    The buyer gets 1% of the advertised price as a bonus from the seller. For example, on a Rs 10,000 item the buyer receives Rs 100 — so the buyer pays only Rs 9,900. On Rs 50,000, the buyer receives Rs 500. The exact figures are calculated and shown on every ad, so there is no confusion. Confirm the 1% in the comments or on the call before you finalise the deal.

    Direct contact: no middleman, no barrier

    A marketplace works when people can reach each other directly. So a seller can give separate call and WhatsApp numbers, and can show them to everyone or only to a serious buyer. When a buyer leaves their number, the seller can call or WhatsApp them back — contact runs both ways, directly and simply.

    Restaurants — Best Restaurant Food & Directory

    Restaurants — Sirf Restaurants Ka Khaana, Muqabla Ke Saath

    Only restaurants live on this page. First compare restaurant food honestly — which type cooks the best dish, at which price band, and why. Then, below the guide, restaurant owners post their own place in the shared directory: food photo or video, signature dish, and the one answer no listing can skip — “Why is mine better?”

    Best Restaurant Food — Restaurant Types Compared

    Going out to eat — or ordering in — always ends at the same question: which kind of restaurant, and which dish? These six types run Pakistan's food streets. None of them wins everything: each one wins its own plate.

    Why compare? The wrong restaurant wastes the whole meal — a heavy karahi when the family wanted a light treat, fast food when guests deserved a real dawat. Match the restaurant to the moment and the dish to the restaurant, and the money is never wasted.

    Restaurant typeBest dishPrice bandWhy it wins or loses
    Desi restaurantChicken karahi & chicken biryaniMidThe family winner: real desi taste cooked fresh in the karahi, dishes the whole table shares, and a bill a family can pay. It loses on speed and show — no fancy seating, and a fresh karahi takes its time.
    BBQ & grill houseMalai boti, tikka & seekh kababMidCharcoal smoke is a flavour no kitchen gas can copy — the plate for guests, parties and evening treats. It loses as daily food: rich, heavy, and it needs the grill master's hand to stay good.
    Fast food (burgers & pizza)Loaded burger & thin-crust pizzaMidFast, standardised and loved by children — the same taste in every branch, ready in minutes. It loses on health and value: fried, heavy, and the price per person quietly beats a desi family meal.
    Chinese restaurantChicken Manchurian & egg fried riceMidThe change-of-taste winner: hot, saucy, wok-cooked food that breaks the daily desi routine, and most families share the plates happily. It loses where cooks drown it in sauce and salt — a bad Chinese kitchen hides everything under the sauce.
    Dhaba / highway restaurantDaal fry, paratha & doodh patti chaiLowThe honest budget plate: fresh roti off the tawa, daal with a real tarka, and chai that city cafés cannot match — at the lowest band here. It loses on comfort and hygiene standards: charpoy seating and open kitchens are not for every family or every guest.
    Breakfast & sweets houseHalwa puri & paya / siri payaLowThe morning winner: a weekend halwa puri or a slow-cooked paya is a tradition no other type can serve. It loses on the clock — miss the morning and the best of it is gone, and it is no place for a dinner plan.

    BEST CHOICE Best for a family dinner: a desi restaurant. Reason: fresh karahi and biryani the whole table shares, real taste, and a mid-band bill — the surest family plate outside home.

    BEST CHOICE Best on a budget: a good dhaba. Reason: tawa-fresh roti, tarka daal and doodh patti at the lowest band — honest food, honestly priced.

    BEST CHOICE Best for guests and treats: a BBQ & grill house. Reason: charcoal smoke is the flavour of a celebration — the food and the occasion arrive together.

    Best restaurant food — karahi, BBQ & more taste testsWatch on YouTube Restaurant food comparisons & rankingsRead blogs on Chrome

    Reference: General food knowledge of Pakistani restaurants and dhabas — taste, freshness and the occasion decide the plate. Prices move by city and restaurant, so this guide uses price bands only — check the fresh price before you order.

    Questions

    Frequently asked questions

    The page is not opening in WhatsApp — what do I do?

    WhatsApp's built-in viewer sometimes blocks pages — that is a WhatsApp problem, not a Success Hub problem. Copy the link, open your Chrome browser, paste the link there and it will open. On Android you can also tap the ⋮ menu inside WhatsApp and choose “Open in Chrome” / “Open in browser”.

    The page opens very slowly — how can I make it faster?

    Success Hub is one single lightweight page with no heavy downloads, so on a slow connection: wait a few seconds on first load, avoid reloading again and again, and prefer Chrome over in-app viewers (WhatsApp, Facebook). Once it has loaded once, your browser keeps a copy and it opens much faster next time.

    The text looks too small, too big, or the colours look wrong

    The page follows your phone's own settings. Text size: change it in your browser or phone display settings and the page adjusts. Colours: the page automatically matches your phone's light or dark mode — switch your phone's dark mode on or off and the page follows. If the page ever looks zoomed or cut off, rotate the phone back to portrait and double-tap the screen to reset the zoom.

    I can't find the tool I need

    Use the “Find a tool” search box at the top of the Tools section — type part of the tool's name, like “caption”, “password”, “discount”, “zakat” or “whatsapp”, and only matching tools stay on screen. Clear the box to see all 18 tools again. On a phone, the tool buttons sit above the tool form, so scroll up a little after picking one.

    The Copy button is not copying my result

    Some in-app browsers (inside WhatsApp or Facebook) block the copy button. Two easy fixes: open the page in Chrome instead, or long-press on the result text, tap “Select all”, then “Copy” — that always works.

    Is Success Hub free to use?

    Yes. All 18 tools, the earnings calculator, the daily mission and the focus timer are free with no sign-up and no usage caps. Pro plans arrive in Week 3 of the launch roadmap for power users who want premium templates, keyword packs and new tools first.

    Who created Success Hub?

    Success Hub was created by Raja Umair, the creator of ToolMint, as an all-in-one hub for growing a page or business, ranking on Google and earning online.

    What is new on Success Hub every day?

    A fresh success mission, a focus tool of the day, a new growth tip, a new shopping tip and a daily Rank Power task unlock every day at 12:01 AM — the countdown in the Daily Mission section shows exactly when the next set lands. New tools and guides arrive in updates: recent additions include the WhatsApp Business Message Maker, the Mobile Buying Guide, the Islamic Collection and the Success AI Helper — see the What's New section.

    How does Success Hub help my website rank on Google?

    The SEO Title & Meta Writer and Keyword Ideas Finder help you target the exact phrases people search for, the guides teach the 30-day ranking basics, and this page itself is built with the same recipe: keyword-rich titles, structured data, fast loading and genuinely helpful content.

    How can I earn money with these tools?

    Two proven routes: sell services (captions, bios, product descriptions, content plans for local businesses) or grow your own page and sell a product. The earnings calculator shows the math, and the first guide above gives the step-by-step.

    When can I buy Pro or Creator Studio?

    Payments connect in Week 3 of the launch roadmap. Until checkout opens, everything on this page is free — the smart move is to start earning with the free tools now and upgrade when Pro launches.

    Which company makes the best clothing?

    For quality alone, Gul Ahmed is number 1. For design and prints, Khaadi leads. For good quality at a low price, Bonanza Satrangi is best — especially in a sale. The full ranking with the reason for each brand, and the Khaadi vs Bonanza comparison, are in the Shopping Guide section, with YouTube help links.

    How do I get the highest quality and the lowest price together?

    The formula is simple: buy branded items in the sale season, compare the price in 3 places, and never compromise on quality for things you use every day. The Shopping Guide's Golden Rules and ranked lists are built on exactly this formula.

    How does the Discount & Profit Calculator help me save money while shopping?

    Before you buy anything on sale, open the Discount & Profit Calculator in the Tools section and pick Discount mode: enter the original price and the discount % and it instantly shows the final price in PKR and exactly how much you save — so a big “50% OFF” tag can never fool you, and you can compare two sales fairly. If you run a shop, switch to Profit mode: enter your cost price and selling price to see your profit and profit margin % before you fix a price.

    How do I contact the owner? What is the official email?

    The official email of Success Hub's owner, Raja Umair, is umairsaqib211@gmail.com — use it for business questions, sponsorship, or a new tool suggestion. The full security and earnings setup is in the Owner & Earnings section.

    Is my information safe here? Can anything be hacked?

The site itself sits in the owner's own hosting account, signed in with his email, and Google's 2-Step Verification is its real protection. If anyone uses Success Hub's name to ask you for a password or a code, that is fraud — never give it.

That is why the Rank Power system exists — your real daily visits and shares are the power behind both ranking and earning.

    How can I help the site rank?

    The Rank Power section gives one small task each day — visit daily, use a tool for real work, and tell friends the full name “Success Hub by Raja Umair”. No fake tricks are needed: real people and real use are what Google ranks.

    What should I check before buying a mobile phone?

    The Mobile Buying Guide in the Shopping Guide has a ranked list for every budget. Three checks are essential: buy only a phone with an official warranty, match the IMEI on the box and the phone, and compare the price in 3 shops. Buying in a sale? Work out the real final price with the Discount Calculator first.

    How do I post an ad in the Bazaar?

    Go to the Buy & Sell Bazaar, and in the “Post Your Ad” form add 1 photo of your item, its name and price, your name, a call number, a separate WhatsApp number if you have one, and your location (city + area). Choose there who can see your number — everyone, or serious buyers only — then tap “Post My Ad”. Your ad appears in the Bazaar at once and people can call or WhatsApp you. Note: the ad is live for this visit only; closing or refreshing the page removes it, so you would post it again next visit.

    What is the 1% rule — how does the buyer receive 1%?

    On every deal, the buyer (purchaser) receives 1% of the advertised price, and the seller pays it — it is the Bazaar's firm rule, written on every ad. For example, on a Rs 10,000 item the buyer receives Rs 100 and pays Rs 9,900; on Rs 50,000 the buyer receives Rs 500. Confirm the 1% on the call or in the comments before you finalise the deal.

    How do I contact a seller? What are the comments for?

    Every ad shows the seller's call number, WhatsApp number (if a separate one was given) and location: call them, or chat on WhatsApp — no middleman, direct contact. If the seller kept the number for “serious buyers only”, give your name and your number first — their number opens for you, and the seller receives your number too, so they can contact you back. On every ad you can also fill in the “give the seller your number” box, and you can add an optional number with a comment. Ask your questions in the comments first (price, condition, location) — that is how buyer and seller get to know each other before the deal. Always see the item, meet in a public place, and never send an advance payment to a stranger.

    Can I give separate call and WhatsApp numbers? Must my number be shown to everyone?

    No, it is your choice. When posting an ad you can give a different call number and WhatsApp number; if they are the same, leave the WhatsApp box empty and the call number does both jobs. Then choose one of two options: “Show to everyone”, where every visitor sees the number and can contact you at once, or “Serious buyers only”, where the number stays hidden (masked) — only a buyer who gives their own name and number can see it, and you receive that buyer's number too, so you can contact them.

    I am a buyer — how do I give the seller my number so they can contact me?

    Every ad has a “give the seller your number” box: write your name and mobile number, and the seller will see it on the ad under “Buyers who left their number”, and can call or WhatsApp you. You can also add an optional number when you comment — the seller sees it with your comment. Give your number only to a seller you genuinely intend to deal with.

    How do I ask for help in Madad House with a photo or video?

    Go to Madad House and use the “Post Your Help Appeal” form: tap “Open Camera — Take Photo” or “Open Camera — Record Video” — the camera opens right inside the page (tap “Allow” if the browser asks); take your photo, or record 30–60 seconds in your own voice — your name, your city, and what help you need. If the live camera cannot open on your phone, the “Phone Camera” and “Gallery” buttons under it do the same job. Then write your headline, choose the help type (ration, medical, rent, education, clothes, job or other), write your story honestly in your own words, add the amount if you need money, your name, city, and your call / WhatsApp number, and choose who can see your number. Tap “Post My Help Appeal” and your appeal is saved on the shared Madad House system — every visitor on every Success Hub link can see it, open its full detail, comment, and contact you directly, until you delete it yourself.

    I want to help someone — how do I help through Madad House?

    Open Madad House and read the appeals: open “Full Detail & Comments” on any appeal to read the complete story, see the exact need and city, and watch the person's video — every photo opens full-screen with zoom, and every video has play / pause, a seek bar, a Sound slider with mute, and a full-screen button, so you can see and hear everything clearly. Then help in the way that suits you: call or WhatsApp the person directly with the buttons on the appeal, leave your name and number in the “I Want to Help” box so the person can contact you back, or write a comment — a question, an encouragement, or what you helped with. Give your help directly to the person, never through a stranger in between, and never pay any “fee” anyone demands in the name of help.

    How does the Marriage Center (Rishta) work?

    Go to the Marriage Center and use the “Post Your Rishta Profile” form: add a clear photo (camera or gallery), choose “I am” (Girl / Boy) and “Looking for” (Bride / Groom), then write the name, age, education, profession, city, family details and a short introduction. Add your call / WhatsApp number and choose who can see it — everyone, or serious families only (your number then stays hidden until a visitor gives their own name and number first). Tap “Post My Rishta Profile” and your profile is saved on the shared system — every visitor on every Success Hub link can see it, open its full detail, comment on it, and contact you directly, until you delete it yourself. Families looking for a rishta: search the profiles, read the full detail, ask questions in the comments, and always meet and verify in person before any decision. Never pay any “rishta fee” to anyone.

    How do I ask for free food for my family?

    Go to Free Food for the Poor and use the “Post Your Free Food Appeal” form: tap “Open Camera — Take Photo” or “Open Camera — Record Video” — the camera opens right inside the page (tap “Allow” if the browser asks) — take your photo, or record 30–60 seconds in your own voice: your name, your city, how many family members you have, and what food you need. If the live camera cannot open on your phone, the “Phone Camera” and “Gallery” buttons under it do the same job, and you can also add a voice note. Then write your name, family members, city and area, what food you need, and your call / WhatsApp number, and choose who can see your number. Tap “Post My Free Food Appeal” and your appeal is saved on the shared system — every visitor on every Success Hub link can see it, open its full detail, comment, and contact you directly to give free food, until you delete it yourself.

    I want to give free food — how do I help a needy family?

    Open Free Food for the Poor and read the appeals: open “Full Detail” on any appeal to see the family size, the city and area, and exactly what food is needed — every photo opens full-screen with zoom, and every video has play / pause, a seek bar, a Sound slider and a full-screen button. Then call or WhatsApp the family directly with the buttons on the appeal and give the food yourself — cooked food, a ration bag, or food arranged at a shop near them. Write in the comments what you gave, so others are encouraged too. Give food directly to the family, never through a stranger in between, and never pay any “fee” anyone demands in the name of help.

    How do I delete my appeal?

    Only you can delete it — open it on the same phone/browser you posted from and tap Delete. The Delete button appears only on the phone/browser the appeal was posted from, so nobody else can delete your appeal. Tapping Delete first asks “Are you sure? This cannot be undone” — confirm, and the appeal is removed completely, together with its photo and video. The same owner-only Delete works on your own ads in the Bazaar too.

    How do I keep Success Hub permanent on my phone, in Chrome?

    Three steps, also shown in the Success City section at the top: (1) open the site in the Chrome browser, not inside WhatsApp or Facebook; (2) in Chrome tap the ⋮ menu and choose “Add to Home screen” — Success Hub then opens from your home screen like an app; (3) to find it again any time, search its full name, “Success Hub by Raja Umair”, on Google. The site's permanent address never changes, so a saved home-screen icon or bookmark keeps working.

    Does Success Hub work on my phone?

    Yes — Success Hub is built lightweight with no heavy downloads, so it opens fast on any phone and any connection, and every tool is fully usable on a small screen.
